The FOMC’s January 27, 2021 statement keeps policy highly accommodative (rates at 0–0.25%, ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases) given a recovery that has moderated and remains dependent on the virus and vaccination progress. Beige Book insights point to a mixed but still fragile backdrop: service industries—especially hospitality and travel—remain hard hit and constrained by COVID-19 cases and restrictions, and regional labor markets have softened in these segments. Offsetting pockets of strength include firmer labor demand in manufacturing, construction, and transportation, vaccine-driven business optimism for 2021, and signs of solid activity in some real estate categories. Layering in credit dynamics, SLOOS indicates tighter standards and soft demand for C&I loans (a headwind for business credit), partially offset by easing in several mortgage categories, expectations for stronger consumer loan demand at small banks, and firmer C&I demand at foreign banks. Net: policy support is strong, but service-sector weakness and constrained firm borrowing keep the tone slightly negative, albeit tempered by vaccine-led optimism and sectoral strength.
